treatment_protocol_ch1: Tissue dissociation: Human skin tumor biopsies (4mm punch) were dissociated into single-cell suspensions using the Miltenyi Biotec human tumor dissociation kit. Tissue punches were received on ice in biopsy transport media (PBS + FBS + antibiotics). Enzymes H, R, and A were reconstituted following the manufacturer's instructions and mixed with Pre-warmed RPMI 1640 medium. Biopsies were minced into 1-2mm pieces, transferred to enzyme mix, and incubated at 37°C for 30 minutes at 800 rpm in a thermomixer. Following incubation, samples were pipetted to break up clumps and filtered through a 70µm cell strainer into a 50ml conical tube. Tubes were centrifuged at 1500 rpm for 10 minutes at 4°C, and cells were resuspended in cold PBS. Cell viability and concentration were assessed using trypan blue and a cell counting slide. Cells were pelleted again and resuspended in a 1:1 mixture of FBS and FBS + 20% DMSO for cryoPreservation. Cryovials were stored at -80°C overnight before transferring to liquid nitrogen storage.
extract_protocol_ch1: CryoPreserved peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) were thawed, labeled, and Prepared for 10x droplet encapsulation following a modified protocol adapted from 10x and BioLegend TotalSeq C protocols. The PBMCs were thawed in a 37°C water bath, and the cell number and viability were assessed using Trypan Blue staining. Cells were blocked using Human TruStain FcX™ Fc blocking reagent and stained with TotalSeq™ C antibodies and hashing antibodies. Live cells were sorted using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) with the gates set for CD45+ and CD3+ cells. The sorted cells were combined with CD3- cells to maintain a 1:3 ratio and cryoPreserved in Bambacker Preservation medium with SUPERase•In™ RNase Inhibitor. Equal volumes of five hashed samples were combined, ensuring that samples stained with the same hashing antibody were not mixed. The cells were slow-frozen at -80°C before being transferred to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. Thawing and final sample Preparation for encapsulation were performed immediately before loading onto the 10x 5’ v2 Chromium platform. Sequencing parameters were set for 5' cDNA, a/b VDJ, g/d VDJ, and ADT libraries according to the targeted cell number for single-cell RNA sequencing.
data_processing: scRNA-seq Pre-processing: The GRCh38.p13 primary assembly from Ensembl Release 98 and the GENCODE v32 primary assembly were modified as follows. The sequence headers in the Ensembl FASTA were modified to match the primary assembly from GENCODE, by replacing metadata with original contig names, appending "chr" to names of autosomes and sex chromosomes, and handle the mitochondrial chromosome. The GTF file was modified to remove the version suffixes from transcript, gene, and exon IDs to match Previous CellRanger references. The GTF file was further filtered to include genes passing one or more of allowable gene_type, allowable transcript_type, no "PAR" tag, or no "readthrough_transcript" tag. Cellranger 6.1.0 was used to create a reference for scRNA-seq alignment. The MCPyV sequence was added to the primary assembly and to the final GTF file.

FASTQ files containing gene exPression and feature barcodes were aligned to the human hg38 genome and MCPyV genome using CellRanger 6.1.0. Ambient RNA was removed using the CellBender pipeline. Processed read counts for each sample were imported as a Seruat object after which TCR-seq data was added. We then filtered the data based on mitochondrial reads (25% cutoff) and minimum RNA genes (200 genes). Doublets were removed using DoubletFinder, and cells were annotated with ProjectTILS and SingleR, using Monaco and HPCA reference datasets. The data were merged into a single Seurat object. We performed standard Seurat (4.0) clustering, Harmony batch correction, and manual cell cluster annotation based on marker genes, including transcription factors, effector molecules, and Previously annotated cell types. The data were subset by major cell types and subclustered. Contaminating cells were filtered out based on marker gene exPression. Differential gene exPression, gene enrichment, and GSVA were performed, followed by comparison of cell type proportions, analysis of TCR clonotype exPression, and TCR linkage analysis.
